verses.text: In the days to come, the mountain of the LORD’s temple will be established as the highest mountain, lifted above the hills. Peoples will stream to it.

Many nations will say, “Come, let’s go up to the LORD’s mountain, to the house of Jacob’s God. He will teach us his ways, and we will walk in his paths.” The law will go out from Zion, and the LORD’s word from Jerusalem.

He will judge between many peoples and settle disputes for mighty nations far away. They will hammer their swords into plow blades and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation won’t attack nation with a sword, and people won’t train for war anymore.
Everyone will sit under their own vine and fig tree, and no one will make them afraid. The LORD of Armies has spoken.
Even if other nations follow their own gods, we will follow the name of the LORD our God forever.
“On that day,” says the LORD, “I will gather those who are lame, those who were driven away, and those I have afflicted.
“I will make the lame a remnant and those sent far away a strong nation. The LORD will rule over them on Mount Zion from then on and forever.
“You, watchtower of the flock, hill of daughter Zion, your former rule will return to you—the kingdom of daughter Jerusalem.”
Why are you crying out so loudly? Is there no king among you? Has your counselor died, so that pain grips you like a woman in labor?

“Suffer and labor to give birth, daughter Zion, like a woman in labor. You must leave the city and live in the open country. You will go to Babylon, but there you will be rescued; there the LORD will redeem you from your enemies.”
Now many nations have gathered against you, saying, “Let her be defiled! Let us watch Zion’s downfall with satisfaction!”
But they don’t know the LORD’s thoughts or understand his plan: he has gathered them like sheaves on a threshing floor.

“Rise and thresh, daughter Zion! I will make your horns iron and your hooves bronze. You will crush many peoples, and I will dedicate their gain to the LORD, their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.”
